policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'for thee' does not distinguish the qere לָךְ from the ketiv לכי; both candidates remain compatible, so the documented qere base remains the fallback.
ASV 'thy neighbors' does not distinguish the qere שְׁכֵנָיִךְ from the ketiv שכנכי; both candidates remain compatible, so the documented qere base remains the fallback.
ASV 'she poured out' does not distinguish the qere מוֹצָקֶת from the ketiv מיצקת; both candidates remain compatible, so the documented qere base remains the fallback.
ASV 'thy debt' does not distinguish the qere נִשְׁיֵךְ from the ketiv נשיכי; both candidates remain compatible, so the documented qere base remains the fallback.
ASV 'thy sons' does not distinguish the qere וּבָנַיִךְ from the ketiv בניכי; both candidates remain compatible, so the documented qere base remains the fallback.

ASV 'thou' does not distinguish the qere אַתְּ from the ketiv אתי. The mapped Hebrew-gloss note concerns 'liveth (or, reviveth)' elsewhere in the verse and does not decide this unit; both candidates remain compatible, so the documented qere base remains the fallback.

ASV 'thou' does not distinguish the qere אַתְּ from the ketiv אתי. The mapped Hebrew-gloss note 'Peace' concerns the woman's reply and does not decide this unit; both candidates remain compatible, so the documented qere base remains the fallback.

ASV 'wilt thou go' explicitly renders a second-person feminine form, selecting qere הֹלֶכֶת over ketiv הלכתי, which is first person. The mapped Hebrew-gloss note 'Peace' concerns the woman's reply and does not affect this unit.

ASV 'his hands upon his hands' explicitly renders the plural, selecting qere כַּפָּיו over singular ketiv כפו. The alternative-rendering note 'bowed himself' concerns English wording elsewhere and cannot decide this reading.
